notes: opt/node is the general-purpose Node runtime exposed to command tools; the Playwright driver keeps a separate architecture-matched node.exe.
The ia32 pack ships a 32-bit Node runtime: a 32-bit Windows host cannot start x64 node.exe, so everything in this pack must be 32-bit.
x86 node.exe still runs on 64-bit Windows under WOW64, so this pack stays usable on a 64-bit host without carrying a second runtime.
The native esbuild package is architecture-specific; the ia32 pack must carry @esbuild/win32-ia32, which npm only installs when the runtime it runs under is 32-bit.
The runtime is a production-only npm installation used for the bundled remotion command and offline project bootstrap.

Remotion publishes @remotion/compositor-win32-x64-msvc only. The ia32 pack therefore injects a locally compiled @remotion/compositor-win32-ia32-msvc, the renderer branch that resolves it, and an x264 thread cap, so a 32-bit host can render instead of only editing projects.

ia32.ffmpeg: 7.1 shared libraries built with i686-w64-mingw32 GCC (msvcrt) + static x264
notes: Built from remotion/packages/compositor so the 32-bit binary matches the renderer version.
Emits a Win7-safe PE: no Win10-era imports, LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE set (4GB address space).
x264 thread cap is applied by the renderer patch: >=4K uses 6 threads, >=1440p uses 8; measured peaks without it were 3716MB (4K, encoder OOM) versus 2289MB with the cap.

browser.source: hand-prepared Chrome 109 win32 archive (last Chrome line supporting Windows 7)
browser.note: Chrome 109 win32（最后一个支持 Windows 7 的 Chrome 版本）；archivePath 为空则跳过，包内不含浏览器；浏览器再分发合规性由投喂者自行确认

playwrightNode.note: Playwright 1.40 supports Node >=16 but its win32 wheel carries an x64 node.exe. The ia32 supplement replaces it with this pinned 32-bit Node 16 runtime and validates the PE machine type.

common.description: Slim Win7-friendly common package set with networking, office document IO, image IO, database access, and plotting.

notes: Python 3.8 is the last official CPython line that still supports Windows 7.
The embeddable package is used so the supplement archive can be extracted directly into the desktop install directory.
Windows 7 should include KB2533623 and the Universal CRT update for best compatibility.
The default Python package index is the Tsinghua Tuna mirror for more stable Win7 supplement builds in domestic networks; override it with -PythonPackageIndexUrl when needed.
The Playwright Python driver is pinned in requirements-win7-common.txt (a win32 wheel exists for CPython 3.8), but Chromium is NOT bundled: the Playwright Chromium build requires Windows 10+.

Playwright 1.40's win32 wheel bundles an x64 Node runtime. The ia32 supplement installs the pinned Node 16.20.2 win-x86 runtime over driver/node.exe and validates the PE machine type before packaging.

Node 16 is the minimum runtime supported by the Playwright 1.40 driver and is outside Node's official Windows 7 support matrix; the bridge sets NODE_SKIP_PLATFORM_CHECK=1 and Win7 compatibility must be verified on a real ia32 image.

The build never downloads a browser by itself (Playwright Chromium requires Windows 10+), but a hand-prepared Chrome 109 win32 archive can be staged into opt/browser via the top-level browser section or -BrowserArchivePath; whether the binaries may be redistributed is the feeder's own responsibility to confirm.
On Win7 the browser_* tools must drive a locally installed browser via mode/executable_path/channel; installBrowser stays false so the build never attempts to download Chromium.
To ship a modern browser for Windows out of the box, add a Windows 10+ x64 supplement with installBrowser=true; the Win7 ia32 pack tops out at Chrome 109.
Git for Windows documents 2.46.2 as the last version supporting Windows 7 / 8 / 8.1.
PortableGit ships Git Bash (bash) plus the POSIX toolchain (curl, tar, which, ssh, gzip, less, etc.) so the agent command tool runs in a bash environment.
The PortableGit archive is a 7-Zip self-extracting executable; the build script extracts it silently with -o<dir> -y.
ripgrep is bundled as a standalone binary so search_content can use rg without relying on system installation.

14.1.0 is the last official release that still runs on Windows 7: the i686 14.1.1 binary is built with Rust 1.78+ and statically imports bcryptprimitives.dll (ProcessPrng) plus api-ms-win-core-synch-l1-2-0.dll (WaitOnAddress), so it fails to start on Windows 7 and Git Bash reports a segmentation fault.
Do not bump past 14.1.0 unless the binary is rebuilt with Rust <= 1.77.2; the build now rejects Win8+-only PE imports for rg.
Static FFmpeg 4.4.1 (built 2021, i686-w64-mingw32, gcc 11.2) for Windows 7 compatibility.
Bundles x264, x265, aom, vpx, opus, mp3lame, webp, openjpeg and many other codecs; the gzip asset is decompressed into opt\ffmpeg\bin\ffmpeg.exe during staging.
radare2 console disassembler toolkit (r2, rabin2, radiff2, rafind2, rahash2 and friends).
The release zip has one top-level directory; staging flattens it into opt\r2 so opt\r2\bin\radare2.exe exists and the runtime can prepend it to PATH.
